contracts.query_projection: QB -> 64-head partial RoPE (64/512 rotated). Keep W8A8 output BF16 rounding then original rotary arithmetic and Q pitch. cos/sin must remain the query generation. Compression may reuse the source tables.
contracts.SWA: After required BF16 WKV, fuse 512-wide RMS -> partial 64 RoPE -> strided cache store. Preserve epsilon, rounding, original positions, slot validity and write visibility. 2304 private logical bytes removed per row. No WKV time credited.
contracts.first_projection: QA and index-W share a local BF16 input on the eight index layers only; one avoided read is 10240 bytes per local query row. Clamp by the original W/cast/scale branch and its visible tail versus index-Q rotation. Both GEMMs remain. Joined QA/index-W matched isolated 3/211 rows. Broader tilings and pitches still conditional.
contracts.index_Q: Index-Q rotary -> query quantizer moves rotation to a later invocation. Price the exposed early tail against concurrent index-W and subtract remaining rotary cost if exposed at the later reader. Always keep per-head scale and its rounding, distinct from W8A8 QR. This option is separate from the joint totals.
contracts.compressed_key: After WK keep the 128-wide key RMS, partial rotation, original per-row quantization then key INT8 and FP16 scale. Before changing the 512-wide long latent, WK must finish reading it. Keep independent long page coordinates and all destination writes. Joint totals include key/long interfaces once; pair-only subset is not added.
contracts.excluded: Only the explicitly named QR-share and optimistic-union scenarios credit the previously priced second QR quantizer once. No credit for WKV/QA/QB/secondary matrix duration, changes to placement, QLI itself, inverse output rotary, C2 FP32 pool/ring updates outside the explicitly named C2 scenarios, communication, or host gaps.
contracts.C2_prefix: C2 on layers 2/8/14 can share the FP32 activation tile across independent Wkv/Wgate projections. Optionally absorb the BF16-to-FP32 cast. Retain exact separate FP32 accumulation, old ring reads before conflicting updates, all ring state, BF16 pooled values including positive-zero incomplete rows, then RMS. If hardware cannot feed both FP32 GEMMs without GM staging, the corresponding bytes stay. Separate pool/update/normalization timing includes work still required. through_C2_bytes_and_QR does not include savings on those four vector tasks.

paired_reference_method: Compare max of eight transformed deadlines in each arm; subtract lower/upper credits across independently bounded peer joins for the outer interval. For ordinary requests the denominator is the corresponding measured stock or restored time.
limits: Frozen C8 uses 4 actual eager waves with TP/DP join bounds and one rank-window estimate per scheduled target graph. Keep other arrivals fixed and assume changes transmit to the next EP16 join. Uncaptured host launch relief, interference and unrelated downstream waits can change service time.

joint_bytes uses the same pre-join Q rotary scheduling in both arms; joint_bytes_vs_stock also counts the schedule-only credit. The KV-only stream has no Q join. Combined savings are recomputed via max on the two clocks. No sum of the single-branch effects.

The contiguous-copy rate prices logical intermediate traffic. Cache hits, missing rows, pitches and scatter geometry can alter it. 25/50/100% are net fractions of observed vector/publication task times, including still mandatory computation and stores; the last is deliberately generous. They do not remove either projection. Named internal-gap scenarios additionally assume that a fraction of wall time between consecutive kernels on one stream disappears with their submission. Device gaps can include delayed upstream readiness, synchronization or other submissions. The key-to-long gap is separate and only belongs to a joint multi-output producer. Do not interpret these scenarios as measured host time.

Eager/graph source layers 2,8,14 (C2) and 20 (C1) publish compressed key and long KV. Layers 24,28,32,36 consume previous keys; other 32 layers have no index projections. Local-query-empty branches retain their real cache writes, both-empty branches their original zero/collective obligations.

The eight-request run and six ordinary requests have different histories. Ordinary first prompts interpolate per-layer-group costs over actual nonempty row sizes using the T3/K24 graph as a short anchor; cache shape, launch overhead, and concurrency are proxies. Results use each request’s actual verification count and two measured reference times. Packed A5, different dtype, alternate execution order and unobserved branches retain distinct contracts.

Earlier WKV completion starts QB in the pinned dual-stream schedule. Extending the WKV kernel through all stores without an early completion signal delays QB: the matrix join needs its own reprice. The priced SWA path keeps WKV separate. Moving rotation into the KV writer cannot overwrite the pre-RoPE compressed latent before WK reads it.
